exposure: Area X (elliptical shape formed by interspinal diameter extending into the sacrum and tangent to the top symphysis pubis)
outcome: Type of delivery (vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included mothers who underwent 3D tomography for any reason, consisting of a group who had a vaginal delivery (n=89) and a group who had a cesarean section after labor started (n=19).
finding: The study found no statistically significant differences in pelvic measurements (CD, CO, CA, ISD, and area x values) between participants who had a vaginal delivery and those who had a cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study concluded that there was no direct relationship between pelvic measurements and the type of delivery (mode of birth).
